title: Generating proteins with complex functions - Nature Machine Intelligence
gist: A two-page News & Views item by Microsoft Research's Sarah Alamdari and Kevin K. Yang, whose body text is behind a paywall; only the standfirst is available. It frames a simple generative model that learns protein sequence and structure together with functional context as the enabler of designing proteins with specified molecular functions and multiple structural states, commenting on the ProDiT paper by Jing et al. in the same issue.

insights.claim: A single simple generative model that learns protein sequence and structure together with functional context is sufficient to design proteins with specified molecular functions and multiple structural states.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Architectural simplicity plus joint multimodal training is being endorsed by the journal as the direction of travel in protein design, signalling where research spend and talent will concentrate.
insights.quote: A simple generative model learns protein sequence and structure together with functional context, enabling the design of proteins with specified molecular functions and multiple structural states.

insights.claim: Multiple structural states, not just single static folds, are now treated as a design specification worth commentary in a peer-reviewed venue, via function-conditioned generation strategies illustrated in the piece's single figure.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Designed conformational switching is moving from aspiration to reviewed capability, the precondition for engineered biosensors and regulated enzymes.
insights.quote: Fig. 1: ProDit function conditioned generation strategies.

insights.claim: Microsoft Research protein-ML scientists Sarah Alamdari and Kevin K. Yang, both based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, authored this commentary on multimodal function-conditioned protein generation, declaring no competing interests.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Confirms Microsoft Research as an active voice shaping the protein-generative-model agenda, useful when mapping which large tech labs hold bio-AI expertise.
insights.quote: Microsoft Research, Cambridge, MA, USASarah Alamdari & Kevin K. Yang

insights.claim: The commentary anchors on Jing et al. in Nature Machine Intelligence (doi 10.1038/s42256-026-01329-2) and situates it against prior work including RFdiffusion (Watson et al., Nature 2023), large language models for protein sequences (Madani et al., Nature Biotechnology 2023) and ESM3-era work (Hayes et al., Science 2025).
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Maps the reference set that defines the competitive frontier in generative protein design — the short list to track for capability jumps.
